chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a woman who menstruates while she is in a state of janābah: is ghusl al-janābah upon her? He said: “The ghusl of janābah and menstruation is one.”

key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, as a state entailing ritual rulings
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of ritual impurity due to janābah
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required for janābah
key_terms.وَاحِدٌ: one; meaning a single ghusl suffices here

ai.seo_question: If a woman menstruates while in a state of janābah, does she need a separate ghusl for each?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ritual purity for a woman who menstruates while already in a state of janābah. Imam Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام states that the ghusl for janābah and menstruation is one, indicating that a single ghusl suffices for both states.
